objective: Determine which Server Ops 0.1.2 release-candidate claims, including consent-gated managed update maintenance and content-free quality handoff, are directly supported by current local evidence and preserve the boundary around pending remote lifecycle gates.
scope: strict adapter and loopback health runtime
managed package identity, installer, and default-off privacy

evidence_items.observed_summary: The local receipt records 58 passing tests, package verification, official skill validation, and an outbound-free GitHub Skill publisher dry-run while leaving remote and managed-repair gates pending.

The skill requires consent-gated managed-update maintenance followed by one content-free owner-bound outcome receipt after substantive use, with no default analytics, reporting, project/process transport, or issue submission.
The skill is explicitly local and read-only, excludes production and remote systems, and forbids bypassing typed mutation refusals.
Runtime parsing rejects unknown fields, linked or external explicit adapters, confines configured workspaces, and accepts only credential-free literal-loopback HTTP health URLs.
Health probing uses explicit timeout and response bounds, disables redirects, and evaluates exact configured predicates.
Discovery starts from listeners, requires exact-workspace containment, bounds candidate enrichment, and tolerates process churn.
Public process observations expose an argument count and canonical digest instead of raw argument values, and human command labels strip terminal controls.
Uncertified lifecycle operations produce typed refusals instead of executable process-mutation plans and record the actual provider availability and request/service workspaces.
Stored refusal receipts are bounded, regular-file-only, schema-checked, workspace-bound, and canonical-digest-verified before recovery or apply.
The deterministic versioned manifest binds the release-candidate package files with canonical text handling.
Manifest generation traverses only regular no-follow package entries and refuses linked package roots, children, and manifest outputs before reading or writing targets.

Package verification rejects links, non-regular or oversized files, unexpected ordinary files, changed manifest entries, and untrusted GitHub origin/path/ref metadata while ignoring bounded generated caches.

The custom installer performs bounded no-follow manifest and metadata reads, verifies source and target trees, refuses unmanaged or modified updates, and keeps verified rollback outside active skill discovery.
No lifecycle analytics, reporting, feedback, update check, or installation identity is enabled by default; configured health traffic remains literal loopback.
The public guide distinguishes installation from activation and disclaims certified mutation, production reliability, and complete cross-platform support.
The ledger pins external source revisions and separates adopted patterns from rejected or deferred operational scope.

claims.statement: Server Ops 0.1.2 presents a local, non-production, read-only skill interface and does not advertise a certified mutation provider.
claims.rationale: The skill and public boundary are explicit, and the local structural suite passes.

claims.statement: In the tested cases, adapters fail closed and health probes are credential-free literal-loopback HTTP with bounded, redirect-free exact-predicate behavior.
claims.rationale: Implementation inspection and the passing adapter/health tests support this bounded statement.

claims.statement: On the current Windows candidate, listener discovery is bounded to exact-workspace candidates, public output redacts raw process arguments, and uncertified lifecycle requests return integrity-checked refusal receipts without process mutation in the tested cases.
claims.rationale: The discovery/planner sources and passing subprocess, receipt, and refusal tests directly cover this host-bounded claim.

claims.statement: The release-candidate package has synchronized version identity and a bounded no-follow verified manifest that permits only the expected Ian-Tseng/server-ops GitHub source metadata in the tested cases.
claims.rationale: The manifest verifier, official validator, and origin-negative regression tests pass locally.

claims.statement: On tested temporary registries, the custom installer fails closed on unsafe or modified state and no lifecycle analytics, reporting, feedback, or update transport is enabled by default.
claims.rationale: Installer tests and static source inspection pass; absence of every possible dependency network path was not established by packet interception.

claims.statement: Version 0.1.2 is locally ready for PR publication gates, but remote CI, public release, consumer installation, and live client activation are not yet verified.
claims.rationale: The release receipt records only completed local gates and explicitly lists every pending remote gate.

claims.statement: The local package defines and tests a consent-gated managed-update check plus one content-free owner-bound quality receipt after substantive use, and the repository carries a disabled closed policy plus one thin full-SHA-pinned managed-repair caller, without default outbound transport.
claims.rationale: The current skill, policy, caller, updater, receipt emitter, schema, and lifecycle tests support this local bounded claim; protected environments, hosted execution, host routing, and public issue submission remain separate gates.

claims.statement: Server Ops 0.1.2 behaves correctly on Linux and macOS.
claims.rationale: The public matrix has not run yet; local execution covers Windows only.

limitations.text: Runtime and subprocess evidence currently comes from one Windows host; public Linux and macOS matrix results remain pending.
Version 0.1.2 intentionally implements no certified start, stop, restart, force, or interrupted-mutation provider.
A local publisher dry-run does not establish remote CI, tag immutability, publication, public install, update, or client activation.
Default-off lifecycle transport is supported by source inspection and tests, not runtime packet interception of every dependency path.

unresolved_uncertainties: PR CI and exact merged-main CI have not run.
No public v0.1.2 tag or immutable release exists.
Fresh public Codex and Claude Code install/update have not been observed.
Live Claude Code activation depends on a machine with the Claude executable.
No dynamic packet capture covers every dependency path.
Protected managed-repair environments, hosted canary, agent execution, and draft publication remain unobserved.
